decisions.issues: Minor, retouch if possible: the two palanquins seen through the gate stand on small wheels under their carrying poles (about x 0.22-0.30, y 0.75-0.82). Palanquins are carried, and in 1.2 and 1.5 they rest on legs. The guards carry spears as well as their swords and round shields. Otherwise clean: dusk estate, gatehouse, Nair guards watching the road, a servant lighting wall-niche lamps, road dust and the jackfruit tree. No text. The wide quiet dusk sky across the top has room for the long caption.

Varma's hair knot sits at the back of his crown, not the bible's side knot above the LEFT ear. Otherwise he follows the private-visit look: bare-headed, no turban, crest or spear, the V13 face and moustache, gold necklaces, a cream and gold mundu. He also has a gold-bordered shoulder cloth. The Rani matches her sheet: severe bun with no flowers, white sari with a narrow gold border, gold ear studs. The Prince, about ten, wears a white mundu, a thin gold chain and a small topknot. Ornate and plainer palanquins rest on legs, which is right. The sky above the gate at the upper left has room for the caption.

Minor background details: three palanquins appear beyond the gate opening rather than two just inside it, and Padmini shows little grey threading. Otherwise clean. Padmini matches her sheet and stands on the verandah above the steps: old Kerala drape with no blouse, a white and gold sari, jasmine in her hair, a gold chain, walking stick in hand. She has a set face and looks off-panel left across the courtyard. The open dusk sky between the jackfruit tree and the roof has room for both balloons.

v01, the only candidate, fails on Nagoji's identity. His earring is a stud with a gold drop hanging from it, against the author's ruling of a tiny flush stud. His LEFT sleeve is rolled up, and the forearm shows a crisp circular stamp with a cross or X glyph inside. That reads as an emblem or pseudo-letter, not the bible's blurred, puckered patch, and the script says the brand is seen only when the sleeve is pushed back. There is faint stubble shading on the chin. He is also lit brightly instead of standing in deep shade under the leaves. The composition, costume, bare feet, setting and the sky space at the upper right all work.
decisions.correction: Keep the composition, setting and dusk light of the previous attempt: Nagoji at the left under the great jackfruit tree in the rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash and cream trousers, barefoot, with the gatehouse, guards and lamp-lit verandah behind him and the dusk sky open at the upper right. Fix the following. His ear ornament is a single tiny flush gold stud on the earlobe with NOTHING hanging from it: no drop, bead, pendant or hoop. Both tunic sleeves are down to the wrists, so no brand, scar, tattoo, circular stamp, emblem, symbol or any mark shows on either forearm or hand. His chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble shading; only the thick curled moustache. Put him in deep shade under the jackfruit leaves, with only a little dappled last light on his face. His body turns away onto a narrow side path running off along the edge of the courtyard, one bare foot already on that path, and his head is turned back over his shoulder toward the verandah.

decisions.issues: Continuity with 1.3 is weak. Padmini stands at courtyard level beside the foot of the verandah plinth instead of up on the verandah. She looks right toward the house, where in 1.3 she looks left across the courtyard toward the tree where Nagoji is, and her pose has a slight forward lean. Otherwise this is the closest likeness to her sheet on the page: deep-lined stern face, gold bead chain, ball ear studs, jasmine at a nape coil with grey threading, old drape with no blouse, stick in hand. Lit lamp niches are behind her, the palanquins rest on legs inside the gate, and there is no text. The dusk sky at the upper left and centre has room for the balloon.

Minor only. The King kneels at the foot of the steps, not on them, and his hands are on Padmini's feet. His hair has a few grey-looking highlight strands, and the knot sits toward the back of the head. Padmini's grey is a little heavier than a light threading. The gate guards carry spears and shields where the script asks for swords. Nagoji matches the sheet: turban, tunic, red sash, barefoot, moustache, clean chin and gold stud. Lettering: put the Varma balloon in the sky gap between the jackfruit foliage and the roof (upper middle), and the caption on the clear courtyard floor at bottom left or along the top-left edge.

The staging is reversed. Padmini stands down in the courtyard by the gate, while the Rani, the King and the Prince come DOWN the verandah steps out of her own house. That contradicts 2.1, where Padmini is on the steps and the King bows below her. It also contradicts the script, where the Rani and the Prince come UP the steps from the palanquins. The King is beside the Rani, not between Padmini and her. The figures are otherwise on-model: Padmini has jasmine and her stick; the Rani has a severe bun, no flowers and a white sari with a gold border.
decisions.correction: Staging fix: Padmini stands at the TOP of the short stone steps on the raised front verandah of her own house, leaning on her long walking stick, with the dark timber posts and lamp-lit doorway behind her. The King stands just below her at the foot of the steps, having risen from touching her feet, seen three-quarter from behind so that he sits between her and the courtyard. Beyond him the Senior Rani (no jasmine, hair in a severe bun, white sari with a narrow gold border and short-sleeved white blouse, small gold ear studs) walks with the Prince at her side (small white mundu, thin gold chain, small topknot). Both come UP from the beaten-earth courtyard onto the lowest steps, their faces lifted toward Padmini, with the gatehouse, palanquins and guards behind THEM. Padmini lifts her gaze past the King's shoulder to the Rani. Nobody comes out of the house, and Padmini is never below the others in the courtyard. Keep the dusk light, the lamp niches, the jackfruit tree, everyone's faces and costumes as drawn, and the clear sky in the upper left for the two balloons.

decisions.issues: The cast is the Prince alone, close, but two unscripted adults fill the right half of the frame. One is a bearded man with a white forehead namam and a topknot, arms crossed, who reads as an off-model, bearded Varma. The other is a woman with jasmine and a maroon stitched blouse, who is neither Padmini (no blouse) nor the Rani (no flowers, white blouse). The framing is a medium-full figure, not a close shot. The Prince himself is acceptable.
decisions.correction: Show ONLY the Prince, in a close chest-up shot: the boy fills the right two-thirds of the frame, his face three-quarter toward the left, eyes lifted and fixed on Nagoji just off-panel to the left. At most the soft edge of a cream sleeve shows at the far left edge, with no face. Draw no other adult anywhere in the frame: no bearded man, no woman, no King, no Rani, and no guards close enough to read. Keep the boy exactly as in the neighbouring panels: about ten, with sharp cheekbones and wide watchful eyes, curly black hair in a small topknot, a thin gold chain, bare-chested, a small white mundu, and a faint thin white forehead line or none. Behind him, a soft, low-detail dusk sky and the out-of-focus edge of the tiled verandah roof. Leave the upper-left third of the frame clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: The composition and both figures are good: a low two-shot, the boy looking up, Nagoji looking down in his commander look, and open sky for the balloons. But the brand on Nagoji's bare left forearm is drawn as a crisp dark ring with a glyph inside that reads like a '4' or an 'A', like a tattoo or a letter. That breaks the bible (a pale puckered patch blurred past reading, with no letters or numerals) and the no-pseudo-text rule. There is also slight stubble shading on his jaw, and the ear stud looks pale rather than gold.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: the low-angle two-shot, the Prince at left looking up, Nagoji at right in a rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash and cream trousers looking down at him with a serious face, the gatehouse, guards, verandah and dusk sky behind, and the open sky at the top for the balloons. Fix only these details. Nagoji's tunic sleeves are worn DOWN to the wrists, so the brand and the scar on his LEFT forearm are hidden. Draw no ring, sigil, emblem, tattoo, letter, numeral or dark ink mark anywhere on his arms or skin; if any forearm shows, the brand is only a faint, pale, shapeless patch of raised scar ridges with a thin white scar beside it. His chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble shading, and his ear stud is a tiny flush GOLD stud.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The King is smiling openly rather than hiding his amusement. The Rani and the King wear a white forehead namam that is not on their sheets, though it matches the Prince's. The gate guards are in back view. The ornament along the palanquin valance is decorative, not lettering. The Rani's hand is reaching his shoulder and her fingers are sound. Lettering: put the two Prince balloons in the sky gap above and right of his head, between the tree and the roof, or in the upper left above the gatehouse roof.

Minor only. The Rani's hair has a faint grey sheen not on her sheet. Clear sky above the centre is limited, so the two Rani balloons may need to sit over the upper-left foliage and gate roof, with the caption on the open earth at lower left. Faces and the hand on the shoulder stay clear. Otherwise clean: hand on the Prince's shoulder, both looking off right toward Nagoji, the Prince matches his sheet (forehead mark, topknot, chain), and the courtyard, gate, guards and dusk match 2.5.

v01 mirrors Nagoji's brand onto the wrong arm. His sleeves are rolled up, and the forearm nearest the viewer, which is his RIGHT arm since he faces the camera with the sash over his left shoulder, carries a long scar and a dark, crisp '8'/'B'-shaped brand. The bible puts the brand on the inner LEFT forearm as a pale, puckered patch blurred past reading, and this dark glyph reads as a letter. His chin and jaw also carry grainy stubble shading. The Rani has a small red bindi that she has neither on her sheet nor in 3.1 and 3.3. The composition, setting, sky space for the balloons and his face otherwise work.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact two-shot: Nagoji on the left in profile facing right, rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash over his left shoulder, the Rani on the right facing him with her hands folded at her waist, the same dusk courtyard with the gatehouse, guards and verandah steps, and the open sky at upper centre left clear for the balloons. Change three things. 1) Draw both of Nagoji's tunic sleeves down to his wrists so both forearms are covered and no scar, brand, tattoo or mark of any kind shows on either arm; above all, nothing on his right forearm. 2) Draw his chin and jaw smooth and clean-shaven, with no stubble shading or grain, under the thick curled moustache, with a tiny flush gold stud on the earlobe. 3) Give the Rani a bare forehead with no bindi, dot or mark, exactly as on her sheet: hair pulled back severely into a bun with no flowers, white sari with a narrow gold border, small gold ear studs.

decisions.issues: Clean. Nagoji inclines his head with his hands clasped, and the Rani is already turning away toward the verandah steps and the house. Nagoji is in the commander look, barefoot, with a clean-shaven chin under a curled moustache and a small gold stud. The white scar shows on his LEFT forearm, the correct side, and the brand is not legible. The Rani matches her sheet (no flowers, no mark). The courtyard and dusk light continue from 3.1. Open sky at upper centre takes both balloons.

The staging and setting of v01 are excellent: carved elephant and yali pillars, latticed eaves, a black mirror floor with lamp reflections, the storeroom doorway with clay vessels, the sky square at the top, all six principals and Nagoji apart, barefoot and correct. But Padmini does not match her sheet or the bible row. Her hair is silver, salt-and-pepper grey rather than thick black with a light threading of grey (the prompt explicitly says BLACK), and her face is gaunt and elderly, unlike the full, strong face she has on her sheet and in 1.3 and 2.2 on the verandah. Lesser drift: the Prince has lost the white forehead mark he wears on his sheet and in 3.1. Ramayyan wears a gold ear stud not on his sheet and is fully lit rather than half in shadow.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly: the same raised corner view across the nalukettu, with the sunken court corner in the foreground and the square of evening sky at the top kept low-detail for captions. Keep the carved teak corner pillars with yalis and elephant processions, the latticed ventilation screens, the black oxide floor mirroring the lamps, the open doorway at right onto the dim storeroom of tall clay rice vessels, and every figure's place and pose. Fix Padmini Amma (seated centre right, jasmine, walking stick leaning beside her). She must have the face from her sheet and the verandah panels: a full, strong, broad face in her fifties, with heavy brows, deep lines at the eyes and mouth, and THICK BLACK hair coiled at the nape with fresh jasmine, with at most a few faint grey threads. No silver, white or salt-and-pepper hair, and not a thin, elderly face. Give the Prince the white vertical forehead mark and curly hair in a small neat topknot from his sheet. Draw Ramayyan with no earring and place him half in shadow at the edge of the lamplight, still holding the palm-leaf bundle and stylus.

decisions.issues: Minor only: the King's hair knot sits at the back of the crown rather than clearly above the LEFT ear (the same placement on 4.2 and 4.3, so it is consistent across the page). Otherwise clean: King on a low stool looking up and to the right, amused; Prince on a stool beside him in the same hands-on-knees posture, white mundu, thin gold chain, topknot; courtyard, lamps and storeroom doorway match the setting; roof and sky band at the top takes the three balloons. Nagoji is off-panel up and to the right, where the King is looking.

Minor: the King is standing here, though he was seated on his stool in 4.1 (it reads as him rising to look around), and he wears a gold-bordered upper cloth over one shoulder that 4.1 lacks. Padmini has a little more grey at the front of her hair than the light threading in the spec. Nagoji is correct: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold stud, barefoot. He looks toward Padmini, who has jasmine, a gold chain, the Kerala drape and her stick, and watches the King, who gazes up at the timberwork. The roof and sky band across the top is clear for the two balloons.

Minor: the low door in the storeroom's far corner is a little more visible than 'barely visible' and has a ring handle. A few woven sacks sit on the storeroom floor. The King stands with the same upper cloth as in 4.2. The King's right arm and pointing hand are sound and point across the court into the open doorway, where clay rice vessels taller than a man's waist are visible. The face and moustache match the sheet, with a pearl earring, bare-headed and bare-chested. The sky and roof at top centre-right take the balloon.

Clean. Muted lamp-brown flashback palette with soft irregular edges. Young Varma, gaunt and wide-eyed, with matted hair and a torn dark-brown waist-cloth, no gold, crouches knees-up between clay grain jars. The scene has straw-bound paddy bundles, a woven mat, cobwebs, low beams and slits of light through the plank floor above, with no burlap sacks and no lamp. The low-detail earth wall and ceiling area above and right of the boy takes the off-panel balloon. The tail runs to the top edge, toward the present-day King above.

The only candidate, v01, is not acceptable. (1) The slivers are not separate: the white cloth lying on the mat in the left sliver runs straight into the sleeve of the coin-giving arm in the centre sliver, so the torn gap cuts through one continuous image, against the script's three separate slivers. (2) The left sliver shows a full meal (a rice plate with four side dishes and a folded cloth), not a single bowl of rice pushed away untouched. (3) The palette is saturated orange and, in the right sliver, blue moonlight, not the muted lamp-brown flashback treatment that 4.4 uses on the same page. The guard's metal gauntlet and the large embossed coins are also off for small fanams and a Nair palace guard.
decisions.correction: Make the three slivers three fully independent small images separated by wide torn parchment gaps, with nothing (no limb, cloth, mat or object) crossing from one sliver into the next. LEFT sliver: only a single brass bowl of plain white rice on a woven mat, visibly shoved aside toward the edge of the mat with a few grains spilled, no other dishes, no cloth and no hand or arm. CENTRE sliver: a close-up of hands only, contained wholly within this sliver. A bare-wristed hand with no sleeve enters from the top of the sliver and drops two or three tiny plain gold fanams, each smaller than a fingernail and with no legible marks, into the open palm of a Nair palace guard, who has a bare forearm with only a plain brass bangle (no metal gauntlet or armour) and a sword hilt at his waist. RIGHT sliver: keep the barefoot figure seen from behind, standing with a drawn blade on a moonlit Kerala road between a laterite wall and palms, face unseen. Grade all three slivers in the same muted lamp-brown sepia as the cellar flashback on this page, with the moonlight rendered as pale amber-grey rather than blue. Keep the soft, irregular torn edges and leave a quiet parchment band along the top of all three slivers for two balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor: the boy reads nearer ten than seven, and he wears a pale grimy cloth over his shoulders, where 4.4 showed a gaunt, bare-chested boy in a dark-brown waist-cloth. The gaps in the floor are wider than slits, so the retainers' legs and feet show through, but this reads clearly as feet crossing overhead. The beat is right: a low angle from below, the plank floor, dust in the light, both hands pressed over his mouth, and an earth-walled cellar with jars and paddy bundles. There is no text. Clear space for both off-panel balloons is in the dark planks at upper left (x 0-0.35, y 0-0.3) and on the bare earth wall (x 0.4-0.75, y 0.42-0.6).

Minor: the palette is warm full colour rather than the muted lamp-brown memory palette of 5.1. Young Padmini's white sari has a gold border instead of being plain. Every beat is present: the storeroom, the clay vessels, the post, one torch held by a retainer, retainers with swords and round shields, and an older grey-haired leader with gold earrings and his sword drawn. A knife is held against the throat of the bare-chested husband pinned at the post, with no blood. Young Padmini, unlined, with black hair coiled with jasmine, stands empty-handed facing the leader, and the swaddled infant sleeps in a cloth cradle seen through the doorway. There is no cup and no text, and the hands are sound. Space for the off-panel balloon is on the dark wall above the doorway (x 0.3-0.55, y 0-0.1).

Varma's hair hangs loose in a full mass of curls to his neck, with no knot. This breaks the chapter 17 bible and MUST MATCH lines (bare-headed, hair in a side knot above the LEFT ear) and clashes with every neighbouring Varma panel (4.1, 4.2, 4.3 and 5.5 all show the hair gathered into a knot). Both figures also stand, while 4.1 and 5.5 seat the King on a low stool in this conversation. The Prince is correct: wide eyes, small topknot, thin gold chain and white mundu. The courtyard setting is also correct.
decisions.correction: Marthanda Varma's hair must NOT hang loose: gather all of his black hair into one firm, compact knot above and slightly behind his LEFT ear, as in the neighbouring panels of this scene, with no curls falling to his neck or shoulders, and no turban, crest, headband or crown. Seat them as on the previous page: the King on a low wooden stool and the Prince on a low stool beside him at the left of the frame, not standing. Turn the King's head toward the LEFT edge of the frame, where Padmini sits off panel, so that his left ear, pearl ear drop and the hair knot above it face the viewer. The Prince looks up at his uncle with wide eyes. Keep everything else that worked: Varma's face from his sheet, curled moustache, bare chest, gold necklaces and gold-bordered cream mundu; the Prince's small neat topknot, thin gold chain and white mundu; and the nalukettu courtyard at dusk, with carved yali-and-elephant teak pillars and brass open-wick lamps reflected in the black floor. Leave the open sky and tiled roofs in the upper part of the frame clear and low in detail for one short balloon.

decisions.issues: Inset continuity flaw, accepted because the inset is small and soft-edged: the Pillamar leader in the lower-right inset has a full black beard and dark hair, is seated and carries no sword. That contradicts the grey-haired, beardless, standing leader of 5.2. Young Padmini in the inset wears a red bindi and looks a little older than in 5.2. The main figure is strong: present-day Padmini matches her sheet closely (heavy brows, black hair threaded with grey, coiled with jasmine, gold stud and chain, cream gold-bordered sari with no blouse, walking stick), with a dry, stern expression. The courtyard matches 5.3 and 5.5, the hands are sound and there is no text. The roof and lattice at upper right (x 0.47-0.9, y 0-0.35) give clear room for three balloons away from the inset.

Minor: Varma wears a gold-bordered cream cloth over one shoulder, where the private-scene look is fully bare-chested, and his forehead carries namam lines. The rest is correct. His hair is gathered in a knot behind his left ear, consistent with page 4. His sheet face, curled moustache, pearl ear drop and gold necklaces all match. His smile is a knowing smirk, with eyes that stay guarded. Padmini, on the left, watches him and matches her sheet, with her walking stick. The pair are seated in the same nalukettu courtyard as 5.3 and 5.4. The hands, including Varma's clasped hands, are sound, and there is no text. Ample low-detail space for three balloons is in the sky, roofs and lattice between the two figures (x 0.38-0.62, y 0-0.5).

Minor only. Padmini stands with her stick in hand, while she is seated in 5.5 and 7.2 (the prompt allows the stick in hand). Nagoji is drawn as sharply as Padmini rather than out of focus. His ear ornament is a tiny round gold bead that hangs very slightly; at print size it reads as a stud. Faint shading on his chin, but no beard. The face, moustache, commander costume, bare feet, the hand at the sash and the turning head all match. Varma is off panel to the right, where Padmini is looking. The top band of roof and sky has room for all three balloons.

Varma has a clear silver-grey streak at his temple. That breaks the MUST MATCH line (black hair, never the grey of the sheet's later figure) and clashes with his all-black hair in 5.3, 6.4, 6.5 and 7.1. Everything else works: the stool, the stern turn, bare chest, gold-bordered mundu, necklaces, pearl ear drop, the setting and the roof space at upper right.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition exactly as before. The King sits on the low wooden stool in the lamplit nalukettu courtyard, his torso turned and his eyes cut sideways toward Nagoji off panel, playfulness gone. He is bare-chested in the cream mundu with a gold border, with his gold bead necklaces and pearl ear drop. Carved teak pillar at left, storeroom jars and brass lamps behind, tiled roof and evening sky open at the upper right for balloons. Fix only his hair: it must be entirely jet BLACK, with NO grey, silver or white streak at the temples or anywhere on his head, the same black as in the neighbouring panels. Draw it gathered into a side knot above his LEFT ear.

decisions.issues: None significant. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, sharp features, receding hair with curly sides, plain unbordered white cloth, no forehead mark or sacred thread. His arms are folded over the palm-leaf bundle, with the stylus in hand. He is lit fairly evenly rather than standing at the edge of the lamplight. The upper right sky and roof leave ample room for the balloon.

1) The King is off-model and reads like a bare-headed Nagoji: a voluminous loose curly mane with a crown bun, a thick moustache and a small gold ear stud (Nagoji's marker), instead of the Varma sheet's lean face, hair drawn back into a side knot, and pearl ear drop. 2) The brand on Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm is a dark, tattoo-like stamped emblem with a cross-like mark. The bible calls for a pale puckered patch, not a cross. 3) Nagoji sits cross-legged on the floor, but he stands in 6.1 and 7.2. The King sits on a stone step instead of the stool from 6.2. The Prince, the smoke thread, the setting and the roof space for balloons all work.
decisions.correction: Keep the layout. At left, the King leans forward with his elbows on his knees, and beside him the Prince (about ten, bare-chested, small white mundu, thin gold chain, small neat topknot) leans forward too. A thin thread of smoke from a brass floor lamp drifts sideways across the frame between the King and Nagoji at the right. The tiled roof and sky stay open at the top for balloons. Fix these: (1) The King must have Marthanda Varma's sheet face: lean and narrow, with high cheekbones, a long straight nose and a neat curled moustache. His black hair is drawn back smoothly and tied in a side knot above his LEFT ear, NOT a loose bushy curly mane. He wears his pearl drop earring, NOT a small gold stud, which belongs only to Nagoji. He sits on the same low wooden stool as in the previous panel. (2) Nagoji stands barefoot a few paces to the right, facing the King, in the rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash and cream trousers, as in the panels before and after. He has a clean-shaven chin and a tiny flush gold ear stud. Turn his LEFT forearm so its outer side faces the viewer and the brand is out of sight. Draw no dark ink mark, tattoo, stamped emblem, cross or symbol anywhere on his arms.

decisions.issues: Minor. Both men stand, while the King is seated in 6.4 and 7.1. Varma adds gold armlets, a gold belt and a gold-bordered shoulder cloth not seen in 6.2 and 6.4, though the shoulder cloth also appears in 5.5 and 7.2. His hairline is high, but his face, moustache, pearl ear drop and black hair knot match his sheet. Ramayyan holds out a single rolled leaf tied with saffron thread, with no script on it. The King's hands stay at his sides and his sideways look is dry. Hands are sound. The sky, roof and lattice between the two heads leave room for both balloons.

Minor only. Varma's look is a sceptical sidelong frown more than glittering amusement. His knot sits at the crown toward the left rather than clearly above the left ear. Ramayyan holds his stylus while his fingers rest at the saffron knot, so 'loosening' is implied rather than explicit. Otherwise it is clean: both faces match their sheets, Varma has black hair, no turban and gold necklaces, and Ramayyan has no forehead mark or sacred thread. The setting is the lamplit nalukettu with its black floor. The roof and sky band across the top (x 0.15-0.62, y 0-0.2) leaves room for both balloons.

The only candidate (v01) fails the likeness rules. Marthanda Varma's hair is heavily grey at the temples and sides, which breaks his MUST MATCH line ('black hair, never the grey of the sheet's later figure') and clashes with his black hair in 7.1. His knot is a bun at the back of the head, not a side knot above the left ear. Padmini's hair reads as mostly grey instead of thick black with light grey threading. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold drop, not a flush stud. Nagoji also stands, while every following panel on the page shows him seated. The composition, the Rani's plate (cloth, lit lamp, ivory elephant with gold tusk), the Prince, Ramayyan and the setting all work.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact wide composition, courtyard, evening lamplight, the Rani with her silver plate and the folded cloth, lit lamp and ivory elephant, and the Prince and Ramayyan as drawn, but fix these likeness errors. Marthanda Varma's hair must be entirely jet BLACK with no grey or silver anywhere at the temples, sides or knot, exactly as in the previous panel. Gather it in a side knot above his LEFT ear, not a bun at the back of the head. Padmini Amma's hair must read as thick BLACK hair with only a few fine grey threads, not a grey or salt-and-pepper head, still coiled at the nape with fresh jasmine. Nagoji's ear ornament must be a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging below it. For continuity with the next panels, where Padmini rises and goes to him, show Nagoji seated on the low stone step at the left edge of the court rather than standing: same rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash and cream trousers, barefoot. Keep the dark tiled roof and sky to the right of Varma's head clear for two balloons.

decisions.issues: The only candidate (v01) has the wrong framing. The script asks for a close-up on Nagoji's still, lamplit face with Padmini rising at the panel's edge. The frame is instead a wide two-shot: Nagoji sits cross-legged with his face small in frame, and Padmini stands at full height across the right 40% of the panel, so the beat repeats the staging of 7.4. Padmini also has a red forehead dot that she lacks in 7.4 and on her sheet. Nagoji's ear ornament is a small hanging gold bead rather than a flush stud. The costume, the brand and scar on his left forearm, the setting and the lighting all work.
decisions.correction: Reframe as a close-up. Nagoji's head and shoulders fill the left two-thirds of the frame, turned three-quarters toward the right, lit warm from a brass oil lamp below, his face held very still with a steady gaze. Keep the same rust-red turban, long curly black hair, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, cream tunic and red sash as now, with a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe and nothing hanging from it. At the right edge of the panel, cropped by the frame, show only part of Padmini Amma (shoulder, arm and the side of her face with jasmine in her coiled black hair) as she rises from a low wooden stool, one hand pressing on her walking stick. She has no red dot or any mark on her forehead. No full-length figures. Keep the dark tiled roof and evening sky in the upper left, above Nagoji's turban, as clear low-detail space for a caption.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji's chin shows a faint shadow of texture but reads as clean-shaven. Padmini's two forearms overlap closely and look slightly fused near the elbow, but they read correctly as both hands cupping his face. Nagoji has the thick curled moustache, a flush gold stud, the rust-red turban, tunic and sash, and the long white scar on his left forearm. Padmini has jasmine, black hair with grey threads, no blouse and a strained expression. The setting matches the lamplit nalukettu. The roof band above Nagoji's turban (x 0.1-0.45, y 0-0.16) and right of Padmini's head (x 0.72-0.9, y 0-0.2) gives room for two balloons. The tails point to Padmini's mouth; the letterer may angle them toward the King off-panel.

Minor only. Padmini's hands look somewhat older than her fifties. Her upper hand's fingers wrap under his wrist in a slightly tangled way but still read. Otherwise the beat is clean. It is a tight insert of his LEFT hand turned palm up, with the cream sleeve pushed back and the red sash at the edge. The brand is a pale, raised, ridged patch on the inner wrist with no legible letters, and the long white scar runs up the forearm. Her thumb rests on the brand and her work-rough hands wear gold bangles. Her face is cropped above the frame, so the tails go to the top edge. The upper-left sleeve and upper-centre background (x 0.0-0.65, y 0.0-0.3) take both balloons.

v01 does not show the beat as scripted. Script 8.1 asks for Padmini's face, close. v01 is instead a medium-wide two-shot full of courtyard background. It also breaks staging continuity: Nagoji stands upright and turns away as if walking off, glaring down at her. On page 7 (7.3 to 7.5) and in 8.2 he sits cross-legged on the floor with Padmini bent close to him. The brand is drawn as a round concentric spiral stamp, which reads as a symbol, not the pale puckered patch of ridges. There is also noticeable stubble on his chin and jaw.
decisions.correction: Frame this as a CLOSE-UP of Padmini Amma: her head and shoulders fill most of the frame in three-quarter view, eyes wet but fierce, jaw set, fixed on Nagoji just off the frame edge (at most his cream-sleeved shoulder or the edge of his clean-shaven face may show). In the lower foreground, her work-rough hand tightens around his LEFT wrist, his cream tunic sleeve pushed back. The brand on his inner left forearm is only a pale, puckered patch of raised ridges with no circle, spiral, letters or symbol. Keep the staging of the neighbouring panels: Nagoji sits cross-legged on the black floor and Padmini kneels close in front of him. Nobody stands or walks away. Keep her look as drawn: jasmine in the black nape coil, one gold chain, cream sari with a gold border, no blouse. Keep the lamplit nalukettu at dusk. Leave the top quarter of the frame as dark, low-detail roof shadow or dusk sky for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: The composition and staging of v01 are right. Both sit on the black mirror floor with reflections, Nagoji leans back on his right hand, half pulling away, and Padmini kneels holding his left hand and presses her lips to the scar on his inner left wrist. But Nagoji's ear breaks the bible and the author's ear-stud decision. At native resolution it shows a white or silver stud with a second pearl hanging below it, a drop earring instead of a tiny flush gold stud with nothing hanging. There is also light stubble stippling on his jaw and chin.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, framing and staging unchanged. It is a wide 3:1 strip. Nagoji, in rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash and cream trousers, sits barefoot on the black mirror floor, leaning back on his right hand, face turned away, caught almost pulling away. Padmini Amma kneels with both hands around his LEFT hand and presses her lips to the scar on his inner left wrist. Keep the reflections in the floor, the brass lamps, the carved yali and elephant pillars and the storeroom doorway at right. Fix only Nagoji's ear and chin. On the lobe he wears ONE tiny flush GOLD stud and NOTHING hangs below it: no pearl, no drop, no second bead, no white or silver ornament. His chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble dots or beard shading; only the thick curled moustache.

decisions.issues: Minor issues only. Her hair shows rather more grey streaking than a light threading. Unlike the kneeling 8.2, she is now standing with her stick, which reads as her having risen. The beat is clear: eyes wet with a visible tear, face set like iron, head turning to her left toward the King off-panel. She matches her sheet, with jasmine, gold chain, Kerala drape and stick, in the same lamplit nalukettu. The dusk sky, roof and lattice at upper right and upper centre leave room for both balloons.

The beat is right. The Rani, with no jasmine, a severe bun and a white sari with gold border, touches an oiled fingertip to the forehead of Nagoji, who sits bare-headed with his hair loose and the folded turban in his lap. The silver plate holds a lit brass lamp. The Prince stands beside Nagoji looking up, and Padmini, with jasmine and stick, is at his shoulder. But the forearm crossing his lap toward the viewer is his RIGHT arm, and it carries the pink scar and a scratched brand mark. Coming right after 8.2's kiss on the LEFT wrist, this puts the brand on the wrong arm, against the bible. There is also visible stubble on his jaw and chin.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition, cast and lighting unchanged. At right, the Senior Rani (no jasmine) holds the silver plate with the lit brass lamp and touches one oiled fingertip to Nagoji's forehead, with no painted mark. Nagoji sits on a low stool, bare-headed, his long curly hair loose, the folded rust-red turban in his lap. The bare-chested ten-year-old Prince stands beside him with his face tilted up, and Padmini Amma (jasmine, stick) stands at Nagoji's shoulder. Fix Nagoji's arms. The forearm crossing his lap nearest the viewer is his RIGHT arm and must be smooth and completely unmarked: no scar, no brand, no scratches. The brand and long white scar exist only on the inner LEFT forearm, which here stays hidden under his cream sleeve or beneath the folded turban. Keep his chin and jaw smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble shading, with one tiny flush gold ear stud.

decisions.issues: Nagoji wears the wrong costume. He has the chapter 1 captivity look: a torn ochre sleeveless tunic, a stained dhoti and a bandaged wrist. He should be in the cream tunic, broad red sash and cream trousers he wears throughout this scene. Marks on his bare forearm could read as scratched letters. Varma's hair sits in a top-back bun and is streaked with grey; it should be a side knot above the LEFT ear with black hair. The figures are small, full-length and far apart, so the King's softened face, the point of the panel, does not read.
decisions.correction: Nagoji wears the same costume as in the rest of this scene, NOT captivity rags. He has a long-sleeved cream tunic (the left sleeve down, hiding the brand), a broad red sash and cream trousers, and goes barefoot, with no torn ochre tunic, no stained dhoti and no bandages. He is bare-headed, his long curly black hair loose, holding the folded rust-red turban in one hand. His thick curled moustache sits over a clean-shaven chin, with one tiny flush gold ear stud. Marthanda Varma stands close in front of him. He is bare-chested in a cream mundu with a gold border and gold necklaces. His hair is fully BLACK with no grey, tied in a side knot above his LEFT ear, with no turban or crest. Make his face soft and humbled, eyes moist, head slightly bowed toward Nagoji: nothing of the strategist or warlord. Frame it as a medium two-shot from the waist up so both faces read clearly. Keep the lamplit nalukettu at dusk and the black mirror floor. Leave the upper third as low-detail roof shadow and dusk sky for a caption at top left and a speech balloon near the King.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Varma's knot sits at the crown/back rather than clearly above the left ear. The brand on Nagoji's inner left forearm is drawn as a small reddish spiral-like mark rather than a blurred, puckered patch, but it reads as a scar, not text. The Prince wears a small forehead namam (consistent with 9.4). The beat, costume (cream tunic, red sash, bare-headed, folded turban in hand), clean chin, ear stud and courtyard setting are all correct, and the roof and sky between the two heads can take the three balloons.

Nagoji wears the torn ochre sleeveless captivity tunic with ragged edges instead of the chapter's cream tunic with the broad red sash, which breaks continuity with 8.4, 9.1 and 10.1. Padmini's hair is mostly grey-white, not thick black with a light threading of grey. In the storeroom, Varma's hair is loose rather than in a side knot, and the 'cellar door' is drawn as a floor hatch or crate frame, not the low upright door in the corner.
decisions.correction: Nagoji wears the same costume as the panels before and after: a clean cream long-sleeved tunic with the sleeves rolled to the forearm, the broad red sash, cream trousers, barefoot, bare-headed with his long curly black hair loose and the folded rust-red turban in his hand. He must NOT wear the torn ochre sleeveless captivity tunic with ragged edges. Padmini's coiled hair is thick and BLACK with only a light threading of grey, fresh jasmine at the nape, never grey-white. In the background storeroom, the King is bare-headed with his black hair in a neat side knot above his left ear (not loose). He holds open a LOW upright wooden door set into the far corner wall among the tall clay rice vessels, a door that looks like a plain repair panel and not a floor hatch, trapdoor or crate, and he is beckoning. The Prince hesitates on its threshold, and the Rani (no jasmine, white sari with a narrow gold border) stands at the storeroom doorway glancing back toward Nagoji. Keep the wide composition, Padmini's hand on Nagoji's forearm as she looks up at him, the moonlit lattice shadows on the black floor, and the clear roof shadow high in the frame for two speeches.

decisions.issues: Wrong action: Padmini physically hands Nagoji a tied roll (a palm-leaf or cloth bundle). In the script she gives him the NAME in words. The invented gift also clashes with the King's red-cloth bundle in 9.4. Both of them sit on the floor, which breaks from the standing staging of 9.1 and 9.2. Ramayyan sits lit in the midground between them rather than behind them in the shadows. Faces, costumes, clean chin and ear stud are otherwise fine.
decisions.correction: Nothing passes between Padmini and Nagoji: she gives him the name in words only, and neither of them holds a scroll, roll, bundle or any object between them. Stage it as a continuation of 9.2. Both stand on the black mirror floor of the courtyard at night. Padmini (jasmine at the nape, thick black hair lightly threaded with grey, walking stick in her other hand) stands close at Nagoji's side with her empty hand resting on his forearm, looking up at him as she speaks. Nagoji is bare-headed with his long curly hair loose, in the cream tunic and broad red sash, the folded rust-red turban in his hand, listening, with a thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and a tiny gold ear stud. Ramayyan stands farther back, half in the dark shadow beside a carved pillar, holding a single palm leaf with his stylus poised over it. Keep clear dark roof and wall space in the upper part of the frame for three speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Varma's hair knot sits at the crown/back rather than clearly above the left ear, and he wears a white-and-red forehead namam that 9.1 does not show. The beat is correct: the Prince comes out of the storeroom first with wide eyes and dusty knees, and the King follows with a hand on the boy's shoulder, holding out the red-cloth bundle. Lamps are brass with open flames. The sky and roof at upper right are clear for the balloon.

The conch is engraved on the IVORY GRIP, but the script and the 9.6 inset put it on the steel near the hilt. That makes the prop inconsistent and spoils the inset's reveal. The brand on Nagoji's forearm is a crisp, dark, tattoo-like spiral glyph with a tail, which reads as a logo or emblem, not the pale, puckered, blurred brand in the bible. The rest works: bare-headed, hair loose, cream tunic and red sash, clean chin, ear stud, dagger catching the lamplight, red cloth falling across his lap with the dark sheath beside it, and a low-detail lower corner.
decisions.correction: The ivory grip is plain, smooth polished ivory with gold fittings at guard and pommel and NO engraving, carving or symbol on it. The small conch outline belongs only on the steel just above the guard (it is revealed in the inset 9.6), so keep it tiny or out of view here. The brand on Nagoji's inner LEFT forearm must be a pale, puckered, irregular patch of raised scar ridges blurred past reading, beside the long thin white scar. It must not be a crisp dark tattoo, spiral, swirl, circle or emblem of any kind. Keep everything else as drawn: Nagoji bare-headed with long curly hair loose, cream tunic and broad red sash, seated in the lamplit courtyard, the straight dagger raised in one hand catching the lamplight, the red cloth falling open across his lap and the plain dark wooden sheath in his other hand, the low-detail lower corner for the inset and the quiet roof shadow above for two speeches.

decisions.issues: Wrong framing. The script asks for a TIGHT inset on the conch mark and his fingers closing around the ivory, but this is a medium scene showing Nagoji's whole upper body and face. It also shows the King's hands and gold-bordered mundu holding the red cloth, although the prompt says the King is off panel and 9.5 has the bundle open in Nagoji's own palm. The brand is again a crisp dark tattoo-like spiral. The conch on the steel near the hilt is correct but too small to read.
decisions.correction: This is a TIGHT inset close-up, not a scene. Fill the frame with Nagoji's hands and the dagger only: no face, no head, no other figure, and no other person's hands or clothing (the King is off panel). The red cloth lies open across Nagoji's own left palm. His right fingers close around the plain ivory grip with its gold guard, and the first hand-width of bare polished steel just above the guard shows a small right-spiralling conch outline struck into the metal, plain, unlettered and clearly readable. If any forearm shows, the brand is only a pale, puckered, blurred scar patch, never a dark tattoo or spiral. Lamplight glints on the steel. The background is soft dark shadow, with plain dark space in the upper part of the frame for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor only. The brand on his raised LEFT forearm is a small, crisp reddish spiral near the elbow, not a pale ridged patch a hand's width above the wrist. At wide-shot scale it does not read as lettering. The knife grip reads brass/dark rather than the ivory of 9.5, which is negligible at this size. Otherwise it matches the beat: alone by the elephant pillar, arms raised gathering his hair into a knot, rust-red turban folded at his feet, tunic and red sash, barefoot, moustache, clean chin and gold stud, black floor holding the lamp reflections. The cream dhoti matches the page 9 frames. The night sky and roof at upper right are clear for both captions.

The script asks for a Close shot of his fingertips on the carved elephants. This is a medium over-the-shoulder shot instead. Seen from behind, the arm reaching the pillar is his RIGHT arm, so the brand and scar are on the wrong forearm (the bible says LEFT). The brand is drawn as a dark circular seal with glyph-like squiggles inside, which reads as a stamped emblem or pseudo-writing, not a pale scar patch blurred past reading.
decisions.correction: Make this a true CLOSE-UP. The dark teak pillar, carved with elephants climbing trunk to tail, fills most of the frame and stands on the IMAGE LEFT. Nagoji's LEFT hand and forearm enter from the right side of the frame, fingertips resting lightly on one carved elephant. Show at most a sliver of his left shoulder and the cream tunic sleeve rolled to the elbow, and no face (or only the edge of the moustache). He touches the pillar with his LEFT hand only. If the inner left forearm faces the camera, it shows only one small pale puckered patch of raised scar ridges a hand's width above the wrist. The patch is irregular, blurred and lighter than the skin. It is never a dark tattoo and never a circle, seal, spiral, emblem, glyph or symbol of any kind. Beside it runs ONE long, thin white scar from wrist toward elbow. Keep the warm, burned-low lamplight raking across the carving, the black reflective floor glints, and the same courtyard. Leave the upper third of the frame as deep roof shadow or dark night sky, clear for a long caption.

decisions.issues: The forearm is the centre of this insert, and it is wrong. The arm reaching the pillar is his RIGHT arm (back view, pillar on image right), but the brand belongs on the LEFT. The brand is a crisp black triskelion tattoo, a clear designed symbol and anachronistic for the setting, not a pale ridged burn patch. The scar is two crossing white lines forming an X, but the bible calls for one long thin white scar and says the mark is not a cross. The knife grip is a curved bird-head pommel, unlike the straight ivory grip with gold fittings established on page 9.
decisions.correction: Hip-height close view of Nagoji from behind and slightly to his left. The carved teak elephant pillar stands on the IMAGE LEFT. His LEFT arm reaches to it, fingertips resting on one carved elephant. The conch knife sits tucked in the red sash at his LEFT hip, so the ivory hilt and his fingertips are close together in the frame. The knife grip is plain, straight, smooth ivory (cream-white, never curved or bird-headed) with small gold fittings at guard and pommel. It sits in a plain dark wooden sheath, matching the knife given to him on page 9. If his inner left forearm is visible, it carries only two marks. The first is one small pale puckered patch of raised scar ridges a hand's width above the wrist, irregular and blurred, lighter than the skin. It is never a dark tattoo and never a spiral, triskelion, circle, seal, emblem or any symbol. The second is ONE long, thin white scar running straight from wrist toward elbow, never two crossing lines and never an X. If the arm is turned so the inner forearm is hidden, show no marks at all. Keep the rolled cream tunic sleeve, the red sash, the warm burned-low lamplight, the black reflective floor and the same courtyard. Leave the dark night sky and roof at the top of the frame clear for two medium captions.

decisions.issues: Minor. The framing is waist-up, not a tight face shot, but the beat reads: his face lit by low lamplight, turned up toward the elephants climbing the pillar into the roof dark, hair gathered at the crown. The brand is a dark blotchy mark rather than pale ridges, but it is blurred past reading and correctly placed on the inner LEFT forearm with the white scar. The knife hilt reads brass rather than ivory. Moustache, clean chin, gold stud and the first grey at the temple are all correct. Sky and dark roof at top centre are clear for the short caption.

v01 (the only candidate) has a good composition. Nagoji sits at the verandah edge facing the rain, and Revathi arrives under the eaves at left, rain-damp, with the right costume. The jackfruit tree, rain sheets, lamps and ceiling leave room for three lettering areas. It fails on the brand. A large, sharp red horse-head emblem inside a ring is painted on the outer upper RIGHT arm, in the foreground where every reader will see it. The bible puts the brand only on the inner LEFT forearm, a hand's width above the wrist, as a pale, blurred, puckered patch, and earlier reviews rejected panels for a brand on the wrong arm. Secondary issues: his hair is mostly loose, with only a small clasped knot instead of a clear knot high on the crown, and a red band shows under the mundu's waist fold, as if he still wore a sash.
decisions.correction: Keep this exact composition, lighting and setting. Nagoji sits at the verandah's edge in right-facing profile, watching the rain pour off the eaves, his forearms resting on his raised knee. Revathi arrives at left under the eaves in the indigo and gold sari, her jasmine braid and hair rain-damp. Keep the carved pillars, brass lamps, jackfruit tree, wet courtyard and the ceiling and rain at the top for lettering. Fix his arms: both upper arms and both shoulders are smooth, unmarked skin, with no emblem, horse, ring, tattoo, brand or scar. The brand appears ONLY on the inner LEFT forearm (the far arm here), a hand's width above the wrist, as a small, roughly round, pale patch of puckered scar ridges, blurred past reading, never a horse, symbol, ring or letter, with a long thin white scar beside it running from wrist toward elbow. Keep that forearm turned so the brand is mostly hidden. Gather his long curly black hair into a clear knot high on the crown, tilted slightly forward, as in the LATER LIFE panel of his sheet, with the rest falling behind to his shoulders. Keep the first grey at the temples, the thick curled moustache, the clean-shaven chin and the tiny flush gold ear stud. The plain cream mundu has no red sash or coloured band at the waist; the dark wooden sheath of the ivory-and-gold conch knife is tucked into the cream waist fold.

decisions.issues: Minor: a small red, glyph-like brand mark sits on Nagoji's outer upper LEFT arm. The bible puts the brand on the inner left forearm, though the long white scar on the left forearm is correct. The mark is small at panel scale, and a retouch to remove it would help. Revathi's faint orange parting line and small dark dot match her sheet. Otherwise clean: both sit side by side at the verandah edge, shoulders almost touching, with the rain curtain and jackfruit tree at left. He has the knot on the crown, first grey at the temple, moustache, clean chin and gold stud, the knife is at the mundu fold, and the rain and eaves at the top leave room for her two balloons.

v01 (the only candidate) stages both figures STANDING. Nagoji leans on a railing and Revathi stands a pace behind him by a pillar. That breaks continuity with 11.2, where she sits down beside him, and with 11.5, where he stands up to offer his hand, so the 'He stands' beat would mean nothing. The brand on his left forearm is also drawn as a sharp red curled symbol, like a '6' or a script letter, which reads as pseudo-writing. His face, hair, moustache, clean chin, stud, costume and the rain setting are otherwise correct.
decisions.correction: Restage to continue 11.2 directly, in the same place and light: the raised front verandah under the deep tiled eaves, the rain pouring in sheets with the jackfruit tree beyond, carved pillars and brass lamps behind. Both are SEATED side by side on the verandah's edge, shoulders almost touching, and neither stands and there is no railing. Medium two-shot: Nagoji in profile, eyes on the rain, his forearms on his knees. Revathi sits beside him, turned slightly toward him, quietly watching his profile, in the indigo and gold sari with the jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, bell earrings and sandalwood line. Keep his Ananthan Pillai look: hair in a knot high on the crown with the rest falling behind, first grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold ear stud, plain cream mundu and shoulder cloth, the conch knife sheathed at the waist fold. No marks on his upper arms. If his left forearm shows, the brand is only a small, roughly round, pale, blurred patch of puckered scar ridges a hand's width above the wrist, never a symbol, curl or letter, with a thin white scar beside it. Keep the upper part of the frame (the rain beyond the eaves, or the dark ceiling) clear for one long and one short balloon.

decisions.issues: v01 (the only candidate) has both figures STANDING and facing each other mid-verandah, which contradicts 11.2 (seated together) and 11.5 (he stands only then). Revathi has a distinct RED dot between her brows, which her MUST MATCH forbids (no red dot; she is a widow). The brand on Nagoji's left forearm is a sharp red monogram-like mark that reads as letters. The rain droplets on her skin and the faces are otherwise good.
decisions.correction: Keep the rain droplets beading on Revathi's face, neck and arms like scattered pearls, her rain-damp curls, and the verandah with rain sheets and the jackfruit tree behind. Restage as a close two-shot that continues 11.2 and 11.3. Both are still SEATED side by side on the verandah's edge, and neither stands (he rises only in the next panel). Nagoji turns his head and shoulders toward her and looks at her face. She meets his eyes, composed. Revathi has NO red dot between her brows: only her thin pale sandalwood line at the hairline, with no sindoor in the parting. Keep the indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets and bell earrings. Nagoji keeps the knot high on the crown with the rest of the hair falling behind, first grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, tiny flush gold ear stud, cream shoulder cloth and plain cream mundu. Keep his left forearm turned down or out of frame. If any brand shows, it is only a small, round, pale, blurred patch of puckered scar ridges a hand's width above the left wrist, never a monogram, letter or symbol. Leave the upper part of the frame (the rain beyond the eaves or the dark ceiling) clear for two medium balloons.

decisions.issues: Minor: Revathi stands rather than staying seated. This matches the v01 framing of 12.1, where they stand facing each other with his hand still held out. A faint red Y-shaped mark and a thin white scar line appear on Nagoji's right upper arm instead of his inner left forearm. They are faint enough to read as a scratch, but a retouch would help. Otherwise clean: Nagoji stands holding out his open left hand (sound anatomy) and Revathi looks down at it with her hands folded, not yet taking it. He has the knot on the crown, first grey at the temple, moustache, clean chin, gold stud, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, and the knife at the waist fold. Same verandah, rain and lamps, with rain and eaves at the top left for his balloon.

v01 is the only candidate. It carries over the 11.5 staging well: Nagoji on the left holding his hand out, Revathi on the right, the carved pillar and lit doorways behind her, and the rain. Two faults rule it out. First, a clear red sindoor streak is painted in Revathi's hair parting. MUST MATCH forbids this, and it would mark the widow as married. Second, the script beat is missed: her eyes look sideways and down toward his hand and the floor, not past him to the house's pillars and dark doorways. Smaller faults: the brand is painted as a reddish mark on Nagoji's RIGHT upper arm, when the bible puts it on the inner LEFT forearm. There is light stubble shading on his chin and jaw. The knife hilt is dark instead of ivory with gold fittings.
decisions.correction: Keep this composition: Nagoji at the left under the dripping eaves, his right hand held out palm-up toward her; Revathi at the right in front of the carved timber pillar, with the lamp-lit dark doorways of the house behind her; rain falling in sheets on the left; open rain and eave space in the upper part for three balloons. Fix these points. Revathi turns her head to look back over her shoulder at the carved pillars and dark doorways of the house behind her, a wary, questioning glance. Her eyes are on the house, NOT on Nagoji, his hand or the floor. Her hair parting is plain black with NO red or orange sindoor powder at all, and there is no dot between her brows; the only mark is the thin pale sandalwood line at her hairline. Nagoji's chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble shading. His upper arms and his right forearm carry no marks or brands; the brand and the white scar belong only to the inner LEFT forearm, which may stay out of view. The knife at his waist fold has a pale ivory grip with small gold fittings in a plain dark wooden sheath.

decisions.issues: Minor only. Nagoji's grey at the temple is a broad streak, heavier than 'first grey'. There is very light stubble shading on his jaw, not a beard. The brand is a round mark near the left elbow rather than a hand's width above the wrist. The figures swap sides from 12.1 (Revathi now on the left). The same verandah, rain and costumes carry over, she smiles with her hand in both of his, the knife has an ivory and gold hilt, and there is no sindoor. Open rain and tree space at the upper left suits Revathi's balloon, and the eave ceiling at the top centre suits Nagoji's.

Minor only. A small brass lamp is already burning beside the cellar door, although the storeroom should be lit only by grey rain-light. The cellar door is ajar on its steps and is a little taller than a repair panel, but it is still low and in the far corner, matching the page 4 storeroom. Nagoji's temple grey is a broad streak, and there is light stubble shading on his jaw. The brand on his inner left forearm is a blurred, glyph-like burn, not readable. The beat works: he leads her by the hand between clay rice vessels taller than a man's waist, with rain-light from the doorway behind them. The plain dark plaster wall at the upper right has ample room for the caption.

Minor only. The brand is drawn as a crisp reddish glyph-like mark on Nagoji's RIGHT forearm, when the bible puts it on the inner LEFT forearm; it is not readable as letters. The lamplight is fairly even, with less deep shadow than asked. The beat and setting are right: an earth-walled cellar with low beams, clay grain jars, straw-bound paddy bundles and a woven mat; he sets down a just-lit brass open-wick lamp; Revathi stands at the foot of the steps, which rise to the low door. There is no sindoor. Balloon space is in the low-detail beam ceiling and the earth wall across the upper right, and in the dark stairwell above Revathi.

Minor only. There is light stubble shading on Nagoji's jaw, and his temple grey is fairly broad. A close lamplit two-shot as scripted: Revathi's eyes search his face and her hand rests on his arm. The brand and white scar sit correctly on his inner left forearm. The hands are sound, the cellar matches 12.4, and there is no sindoor or dot. Lettering space is tighter than ideal: use the dark jar-lined shadow above and left of Revathi's head, and the doorway and steps area at the upper right, for the four areas.

Minor. The couple are drawn larger and better lit than the script's 'small and half-lost in the dark', so the clothed kiss shows directly as well as in the merged wall shadow. The lamp sits between the couple and the shadow, so physically the shadow falls the wrong way, which is a common comics cheat. Otherwise clean: Nagoji has the topknot, first grey, curled moustache, clean chin, small gold stud, shoulder cloth and mundu, conch knife and bare feet. Revathi has the indigo sari, jasmine braid, armlets and sandalwood line. The merged shadows on the earth wall carry the beat. There is room for two captions on the upper wall and beams and the lower-right wall.

The brand on his raised left wrist is a crisp red-brown tattoo glyph, like a sun over a crescent or letter. It reads as a symbol or pseudo-letter, not a pale puckered burn scar. A large bare-skin shape lies behind Revathi on the left, between her braid and the jars, and reads as a stray bare limb or body (or a forbidden bolster). Nagoji's chin and jaw also carry stubble shading.
decisions.correction: Draw the brand only as a faint, pale, slightly shiny puckered patch of raised scar ridges on the inner LEFT forearm a hand's width above the wrist, beside the long thin white scar. It is the skin's own tone or a little lighter, with no red, brown or ink lines and no sun, crescent, letter, emblem or symbol shape, so it reads as old burn scar tissue and never as a tattoo. Revathi's fingertip rests on that pale patch. Nothing else lies on the mat behind Revathi: no bare limb, no skin-coloured shape, no bolster or pillow. Keep the warm low lamplight, her head on his chest, his raised left hand, her jasmine braid, the brass lamp at the right, and the clear low-detail area in the upper part of the frame for the caption and her balloon.

decisions.correction: Nagoji wears the Ananthan Pillai costume from the rest of this page and the page before: a plain cream mundu with no gold border and a cream shoulder cloth, bare arms, with NO red sash, NO red or coloured waistband and no tunic. His hair is gathered in a loose Kerala topknot on his crown with first grey at the temples. His chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven with no stubble. Darken the whole panel to near-darkness. The lamp is out, so he is lit only faintly in deep blue-brown shadow, with a cool rim from the hairline of moonlight at the shut door's edges, and his open eyes just catch a glint as he looks up at the low beams. Keep the wide strip composition, the brass lamp in the left foreground with its single thread of smoke from the dark wick, the shut door at the top of the steps, the clay jars and paddy bundles, his bare feet on the woven mat, and the clear dark area above him for three captions.
